title: Microsoft Teams: meeting policy option to automatically block identified external bots
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap and supplied Microsoft notice support the rollout, optional default and policy scope, and the PowerShell reference explicitly documents automatic blocking. Licensing and the experience for blocked participants are appropriately left unresolved; add the supporting navigation source for the full admin-centre path.

claims.claim: Microsoft Teams is extending its existing external-bot controls with an option to automatically block identified external bots.
claims.quote: Extending the admin controls provided for managing external AI bots and regulating their access to your meetings, we are adding the option to automatically block all identified bots.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and GCC.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC"]

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Targeted Release"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Automatic blocking is off until an administrator enables it, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Default state: Off. No changes occur unless an administrator enables the policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft requires no action unless the organisation plans to use automatic blocking.
claims.quote: No action is required unless you plan to use this capability.

claims.claim: The notice says the option is being added to the existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: A new policy option will be added to the existing Manage bots meeting protection settings in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.
claims.quote: The policy can be assigned to specific users or groups through existing Teams meeting policy management.

claims.claim: Enabling the setting prevents identified external meeting bots from joining meetings governed by the assigned policy.
claims.quote: Identified external meeting bots will be prevented from joining meetings governed by the assigned policy.

claims.claim: Existing detection and visibility experiences remain available to organisers and administrators.
claims.quote: Existing bot detection and visibility experiences for organizers and administrators will continue to be available.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Organisations that do not enable blocking retain their current detection and meeting participation behaviour.
claims.quote: Organizations that do not enable this setting will continue to use the current bot detection experience with no change to meeting participation behavior.

claims.claim: The notice was updated on 3 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice gives Targeted Release beginning in mid-September 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Beginning in mid-September 2026 (previously early August) and expected to complete by late September 2026 (previously late August)

claims.claim: The notice gives General Availability (Worldwide) beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by the end of November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 (previously late August) and expected to complete by end of November 2026 (previously late October)

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none; No action is required unless you plan to use this capability.

claims.claim: The notice supplies no separate GCC rollout schedule.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Beginning in mid-September 2026; General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026

claims.claim: The setting is reached in Teams admin center through Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Join and Lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: This setting is present in the Meeting Join and Lobby section of Meeting policies. Look for "Manage external bots and their access to meetings" and select the appropriate option.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/who-can-bypass-meeting-lobby to sources as the supporting navigation reference: it explicitly gives Meetings > Meeting policies > select the policy > Meeting join & lobby. The existing external-bots citation supplies the final setting.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose; What's changing
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode BlockDetectedBots to block detected external meeting bots.
claims.quote: BlockDetectedBots: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.

claims.claim: The external-bots setting is scoped through meeting policies at user or group level.
claims.quote: Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: The existing control can be configured through the default org-wide policy or through a targeted meeting policy for specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature guide lists only Do not detect bots and When detected, require approval before joining, unlike the cmdlet reference which includes automatic blocking.
claims.quote:
| Do not detect bots | AllowBots | Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings. |
| When detected, require approval before joining | RequireApprovalWhenDetected |

claims.claim: The feature guide calls the value for disabling bot detection AllowBots.
claims.quote: | Do not detect bots | AllowBots |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Do not detect bots leaves bots undetected and unmarked, appearing like other external participants.
claims.quote: Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting. They appear as any other external participant in the meetings.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference instead lists AllowAllBots for disabling detection.
claims.quote: AllowAllBots: Don't detect bots; Bots will appear the same as other participants. Standard lobby policies will apply to them.

claims.claim: RequireApprovalWhenDetected is the default value of the existing external-bot policy setting.
claims.quote: RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.claim: Under the approval option, bots are detected, marked in the lobby and held until explicitly admitted.
claims.quote: (default) Bots are detected and marked in the lobby. They're enforced to be in the lobby until explicitly admitted into the meeting.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting assistants may store meeting data in third-party systems outside the organisation's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting assistants may record or transcribe meetings without participants' awareness.
claims.quote: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.claim: Teams detection uses infrastructural and behavioural signals collected during the meeting join process.
claims.quote: Teams uses built-in detection mechanisms to identify external AI bots based on signals collected during the meeting join process. We utilize a combination of infrastructural and behavioral signals

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Some external bots may not be detected.
claims.quote: Some external bots may not be detected.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Detection may misclassify human participants as bots.
claims.quote: Detection may occasionally misclassify human participants as bots.

claims.claim: The existing lobby experience permits admission of misclassified people and marking them This is not a bot.
claims.quote: When you observe this misclassification in the meetings, you can rectify the situation by admitting the participants from the lobby and marking them with "This is not a bot" option.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: The automatic-block option targets detected external bots, not bots detection misses.
claims.quote: BlockDetectedBots: When detected, external third-party meeting bots and meeting assistants are blocked from joining meetings hosted in the organization.

claims.claim: The described change is a restriction on automated participants rather than a new grant of access to an agent or automation.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is introducing a new meeting protection policy that allows administrators to automatically block identified external meeting bots from joining Teams meetings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A licence requirement specific to this automatic-block option is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots BlockDetectedBots licensing Teams Premium; "external bots" "license" "Premium". Read manage-external-bots, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and teams-add-on-licensing/licensing-enhance-teams; no specific licence requirement found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The external-bots feature guide lists no licence prerequisite for the existing setting.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com microsoftteams "external bots" "license" "Premium". Opened and read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots in full; it lists no licence prerequisite.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the supplied notice names a licence or meter for the option.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bots BlockDetectedBots licensing Teams Premium meter. Read the supplied roadmap record and MC1459141 in full, as well as manage-external-bots; neither supplied record names a licence or meter.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter for automatic external-bot blocking.
claims.quote: Searched: "external bots" Teams "meter" billing; Teams external bots BlockDetectedBots licensing Teams Premium meter. Read manage-external-bots, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and Teams Premium licensing; no meter for this option found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether blocked participants receive a lobby admission or organiser-override route.
claims.quote: Searched: "BlockDetectedBots" "lobby" override; Teams BlockDetectedBots blocked bot lobby organizer override notification license billing. Read manage-external-bots, Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and who-can-bypass-meeting-lobby; none describes an override for BlockDetectedBots.

claims.claim: The external-bots feature guide does not specify the administrator role required to edit meeting policies.
claims.quote: Searched the complete https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-external-bots text for role requirements while reading its admin-policy section and the rest of the guide; no named administrator role or role prerequisite appears.

claims.claim: The external-bots feature guide marks its applicability as meetings, not events.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: [checkmark for yes] Meetings [x for no] Events
